title: Data privacy terms in plain English
objective: Learners can explain 8 data privacy terms in plain English and recognise each one in a short workplace example, meeting them one at a time.

recommended.why: One animated card at a time keeps attention on a single term, with an icon, a definition, a workplace example and a progress row that shows where the learner is.

alternative.why: A guided one-at-a-time reveal versus everything at once: pacing versus overview.

assumptions: Definitions are simplified for a general workforce audience and are not legal advice
Each term's theme is the stage of the data lifecycle where it matters most: identify, collect, use, share, store, delete, respond
Lifecycle order follows those stages; A to Z sorts the terms alphabetically, ignoring case
Examples are typical workplace situations, not descriptions of real organisations
units: cards: one term per card, 3.5 s of playback each
checkDescription: Every term appears exactly once, the cards follow the chosen ordering, and card start times increase and stay within the playback duration.

learnerPrompts.predict: Before the card appears: what do you think "data minimisation" asks a team to do?
learnerPrompts.explain: Choose one workplace example and name another term on the cards it also touches, for instance how consent relates to purpose limitation.
